travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise increased caution in the UAE due to the threat of missile or drone attacks from non-state actors. Terrorism remains a concern. The UAE is generally very safe for tourists but strict local laws apply.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: The UAE is a popular destination and most visits are trouble-free. Be aware of local laws — behavior that is acceptable in the UK may be illegal in the UAE.

healthcare.systemType: Mixed public/private (government subsidized for citizens; private for tourists)
healthcare.costForTourists: Healthcare is world-class but expensive. Clinic visit $100-300. Emergency room $500-2,000. Hospital stay $1,000-3,000/night. Major private hospitals require proof of insurance or credit card deposit.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies are widely available across all emirates. Many medications available OTC. Pharmacists commonly speak English.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Dubai and Abu Dhabi have excellent private hospitals. Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi offers international-standard care. Rashid Hospital is Dubai's main trauma center. English is widely spoken in medical settings.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance with comprehensive medical coverage is essential. UAE healthcare costs are among the highest in the region. Emergency air ambulance coverage is recommended.

controlledSubstances.note: Must obtain prior approval from UAE Ministry of Health before entry. Carry original prescription and doctor's letter. Maximum 3-month supply.
Strictly illegal. Even trace amounts of cannabis in bloodstream or luggage can result in imprisonment. Zero tolerance policy.

medications.generalAdvice: The UAE has strict drug laws. Many medications common in Western countries are either banned or require prior approval. Apply to the UAE Ministry of Health for a permit before travel. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's letter and copies of prescriptions.

scams.name: Fake gold / gem dealers
scams.description: Unofficial dealers in and around the Gold Souk sell fake or impure gold, passing it off as 22-24 carat. Certificates of authenticity are fabricated.
scams.avoidance: Only buy from established shops with clear pricing. Check the carat stamp on all pieces. Request a receipt with carat details. Have valuable purchases tested.

scams.name: Taxi overcharging
scams.description: Some taxi drivers, especially unofficial ones, quote flat rates that are 3-5x the metered fare for trips from airports or hotels.
scams.avoidance: Use only official RTA taxis in Dubai (cream colored) or Abu Dhabi taxis (silver/gold). Always insist the meter is used. Use Careem or Uber as alternatives.

scams.name: Timeshare / holiday property pressure sales
scams.description: Tourists are invited to a 'free' presentation and kept for hours under pressure to sign timeshare contracts worth tens of thousands of dollars.
scams.avoidance: Decline any offer of free gifts in exchange for attending a property presentation. There is no free lunch — the cost is hours of high-pressure sales.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIM cards from Etisalat (e&) or du available at airports and malls. ~AED 50-150 ($15-40) for 5-50GB packages. eSIM via Airalo or directly from Etisalat. Note: VoIP apps (WhatsApp calls, Skype, FaceTime) are restricted.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Excellent free WiFi in malls, hotels, cafes, and many public areas. Dubai Metro has WiFi. Most restaurants and cafes offer free WiFi.
connectivity.bestOption: Etisalat tourist SIM from Dubai airport. eSIM for convenience. Note VoIP restrictions — standard calls and SMS work fine.

cultural.tipping: Not obligatory but appreciated. Restaurants: 10-15% if not included in bill. Hotel porters: AED 5-10 per bag. Taxis: round up the fare. Spa/massage: 10-15%.
cultural.dressCode: Dress modestly in public — cover shoulders and knees. Strict enforcement in malls, souks, mosques, and public areas. Swimwear only at beaches and pools. Bikinis at beach are fine. Women are not required to wear abaya but modest clothing is expected.
cultural.greetings: Men greet men with a handshake. Women greet women with cheek kisses. Men and women typically do not shake hands unless the woman extends her hand first. 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you) is the standard greeting.
taboos: Public displays of affection (kissing in public can result in fines or arrest)
Swearing or making offensive gestures in public
Disrespecting Islam or the ruling family
Photographing government buildings, military sites, or people without consent
Eating, drinking, or smoking in public during Ramadan daylight hours
cultural.haggling: Expected in souks (Gold Souk, Spice Souk). Not practiced in malls or modern stores. Start at 50-60% of asking price.

safety.lgbtSafety: LGBTQ+ activity is illegal under UAE law. Same-sex relations can result in imprisonment and deportation. Public displays of affection by same-sex couples carry serious legal risk. Exercise extreme discretion.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe. The UAE is one of the safer countries in the region for solo female travelers. Modest dress is expected. Harassment is uncommon in tourist areas. Avoid unlicensed taxis.
safety.notes: The UAE is one of the safest countries for tourists in terms of crime. The main risks are strict laws that criminalize behavior acceptable elsewhere (alcohol, drugs, PDA, social media criticism of government). Heat can be life-threatening in summer.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US, UK, EU, Australia and many others receive a free 30-day visa on arrival, extendable. GCC citizens have free access.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-April for pleasant temperatures (25-35°C). Avoid June-September (extreme heat, 40-50°C). Ramadan changes the rhythm of the city significantly.

immediate: Stay indoors between 10am and 4pm during summer months
Drink 3-4 liters of water per day — do not wait until thirsty
Wear loose, light-colored, breathable clothing outdoors
Seek air-conditioned spaces — malls, hotels, and metro are free options
Never leave children or pets in parked cars
after: Check on elderly and vulnerable companions
Monitor Dubai Media Office (Twitter/X: @DMOGov) for official heat alerts
Seek medical attention for signs of heat stroke: confusion, no sweating, high body temperature
resources: NCEMA (National Emergency Crisis Management Authority): www.ncema.gov.ae

immediate: Stay indoors and close all windows and doors
Turn off HVAC systems to prevent dust infiltration
If driving, pull over safely and turn on hazard lights — do not continue driving in zero visibility
Wear a dust mask (N95) or cover nose and mouth with cloth if outdoors
Protect eyes with goggles or glasses
after: Check air quality index before going outdoors
Clean dust from vehicles and exposed surfaces
Replace HVAC filters after major sandstorms
resources: UAE National Centre of Meteorology: www.ncm.ae
